title: DON’T TROUBLE THE TEACHER.
paragraphs: DON’T TROUBLE THE TEACHER.
That sentence fell like a hammer.

Not just news.
A verdict.
Jairus had run to Jesus while his daughter was still alive.

Still breathing.
Still warm.
Still possible.
He pushed through the crowd, desperation in every step. A synagogue ruler — a respected man — falling at the feet of a wandering rabbi.
Because when your child is dying, reputation means nothing.
Only hope matters.

“Please come,” Jairus begged.
“My little daughter is dying. Lay Your hands on her so that she may be healed and live.”
— Mark 5:23
And Jesus said yes.
Hope ignited.
But then… something happened that must have felt unbearable.
Jesus stopped.
A woman with twelve years of bleeding touched His garment, and while Jesus paused to heal her, Jairus stood there watching the minutes disappear.
Every parent reading this understands that feeling.

The clock is ticking.
The situation is urgent.
Your miracle feels time-sensitive.
And Jesus stops.
Before the miracle reached Jairus’ house, the messengers arrived.
Their faces already told the story.

“Your daughter is dead.”
Then the sentence that kills faith faster than grief:

“Why trouble the Teacher any further?”
— Mark 5:35
Translation:

It’s too late.
Stop praying.
Stop believing.
Stop hoping.
Some of you have heard that voice before.

After the diagnosis.
After the divorce papers.
After the addiction relapsed again.
After the child stopped answering your calls.
After the dream collapsed.
The world whispers:
“Don’t trouble the Teacher.”
Your mind echoes it.

“It’s over.”
“It’s too far gone.”
“God didn’t come in time.”
But Jesus heard those words too.
And immediately He turned to Jairus.

Not with a lecture.
Not with an explanation.
With a command.

“Do not fear. Only believe.”
— Mark 5:36
Brother. Sister. Hear me.
Faith is not pretending the situation isn’t dead.
Faith is trusting Jesus even when it is.
Jairus kept walking with Christ toward a house filled with mourning.

Professional mourners crying.
Flutes playing funeral music.
People already preparing for burial.
And Jesus said something that sounded almost offensive.
“The child is not dead but sleeping.”
They laughed at Him.
Because to the human eye, death always looks final.
But Jesus stepped into the room anyway.
He took the girl’s lifeless hand.

Cold skin.
Still chest.
Silence.
Then the Creator of life spoke two words in Aramaic:
“Talitha koum.”
Little girl… arise.
And the Gospel of Mark records something stunning.
Immediately.

Not gradually.
Not eventually.
Immediately the girl got up and walked.

Twelve years old.
Alive again.
Death had just been humiliated in a little girl’s bedroom.
But here is the deeper miracle.
Because one day, another body would lie lifeless.
Not Jairus’ daughter.
Jesus.
The Son of God would walk toward another house of grief — a tomb carved into stone.

He would carry the weight of our sin.
Our shame.
Our rebellion.
Our spiritual death.
He was crucified.
Buried.
Silent.
And for three days, the world thought the same thing the messengers told Jairus:
“Don’t trouble the Teacher anymore.”
But on the third day…
The stone moved.
The grave lost its prisoner.
Jesus Christ rose from the dead.
And because He rose, every situation that looks final is now temporary in His hands.

Sin is not final.
Shame is not final.
Your failure is not final.
Even death itself is not final for those who belong to Christ.
The same Savior who took a dead girl’s hand now offers life to anyone who believes.
Maybe your faith feels weak right now.
Maybe your hope feels thin.
Maybe you’re standing in a house filled with grief wondering why Jesus seemed late.
Listen carefully:
Jesus is never late.
He specializes in situations that human logic has already buried.
He walks into rooms people have already given up on.
He touches what religion says is too far gone.
And when He speaks…
Even death must obey.
So today, ignore the voices telling you to stop believing.
Ignore the whispers telling you it’s finished.
Ignore the lie that says God cannot redeem what has already collapsed.
Bring it to Jesus anyway.

Bring the broken marriage.
Bring the addicted son.
Bring the wounded heart.
Bring the dream that feels buried.
Because the Gospel still declares:
The Teacher is not troubled by impossible situations.
And what Jesus touches…
Lives.
Let that declaration be your act of faith today.
Because someone on your timeline may need to hear this today:
It is not over when Jesus is in the room.
